items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers law, in
relation to authorizing political subdivisions and certain public authorities
to establish demonstration programs implementing railroad grade crossing
monitoring systems by means of photo devices; and providing for the repeal of
such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Amd §§135-a & 1803, add §§1170-a & 1633, V & T L; amd §87, Pub Off L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S252

SPONSOR: THOMAS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law and the public officers law,
in relation to authorizing political subdivisions and certain public
authorities to establish demonstration programs implementing railroad
grade crossing monitoring systems by means of photo devices; and provid-
ing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would allow any local or commuter rail authority to adopt a
local law to implement a program to install and operate railroad grade
crossing photo violation-monitoring devices at any railroad sign or
signal.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends section 135-a of the vehicle and traffic
law by defining a railroad grade crossing as a location where railroad
tracks intersect a public or private highway, roadway, or sidewalk.

Section 2 of the bill amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new
section 1170-a, which establishes a demonstration program imposing mone-
tary liability on the owner of a vehicle for the failure of an operator
to comply with section 1170 of this article regarding obedience to
signal to indicate the approach of a train. The liability of the owner
shall not exceed one hundred dollars for each violation; however, the
adjudicating authority may provide for an additional penalty not above
twenty-five dollars for each violation for the failure to respond to a
notice of liability within the prescribed time.

Section 3 of the bill amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding a new
section 1633. The demonstration program will utilize necessary technolo-
gies to ensure that photographs produced by such railroad grade crossing
photo violation monitoring systems shall not include images that identi-
fy the driver, the passengers, or the contents of the vehicle. However,
a notice of liability will not be dismissed solely because a
photograph(s) allows for the identification of the contents of a vehi-
cle.

Notices of liability are not deemed a conviction as an operator, so they
will not result in any points on the owner's driver license, nor will it
be used for motor vehicle insurance purposes. The bill specifies the
procedure required to provide notices of liability to the owner of the
vehicle, as well as the required information contained on the notices.
It shall be a defense to liability that the vehicle was reported to
police as stolen before the time the violation occurred, and that the
railroad signal indications were malfunctioning at the time of the
alleged violation.

Any local authority which adopts a demonstration program must submit an
annual report on the result of the use of a railroad grade crossing
photo violation-monitoring system to the governor, the temporary presi-
dent of the senate, and the speaker of the assembly on or before June 1,
2017, and on the same date in each succeeding year, the program is oper-
able. The report must include but is not limited to the following: a
description of the locations where railroad grade crossing photo viola-
tion-monitoring-systems were used the number, type, and severity of
accidents reported at intersections where a railroad grade crossing
photo violation-monitoring system is used for the year preceding the
installation of the system; the number, type, and severity of accidents
reported at the intersections where a railroad grade crossing photo
violation-monitoring system is used; the number of violations recorded
at each intersection where a railroad grade crossing photo violation-
monitoring system is used and in the aggregate on a daily, weekly and
monthly basis; the total number of notices of liability issued for
violations recorded by the system; the number of fines and the total
amount of fines paid after the first notice of liability issued for
violations recorded by such system; the number of violations adjudicated
and result of such adjudications including breakdowns of dispositions
made for violations recorded by such systems; the total amount of reven-
ue realized by such local authority from such adjudications; expenses
incurred by such local authority in connection with the program; and
quality of the adjudication process and its results.

Section 4 of the bill amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 1 of
section 1803 of the vehicle and traffic law, by exempting the new demon-
stration program from certain rules governing the disposition of fines
and forfeitures.

Section 5 of the bill amends section 1803 of the vehicle and traffic law
by adding a new subdivision 10. Subdivision 10 states that all fines,
penalties, and forfeitures collected under the demonstration program
shall be paid to the county, city, town, or village within whose juris-
diction the subject railroad grade crossing is located.

Section 6 of the bill amends subdivision 2 of section 87 of the public
officers law by adding a new paragraph (q). Paragraph (q) states that
the photographs, microphotographs, videotapes, or other recorded images
prepared by the railroad grade crossing photo violation-monitoring
system may not be subject to FOIL requests.

Section 7 provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to Federal Railroad Administration data, accidents at railroad
grade crossings have decreased over the past decade, except within the
borders of the Empire State. Federal data indicates that from 2004-2014
there have been 371 collisions resulting in 63 deaths and 137 injuries.
In 2013 alone, there were a total of 28 accidents on the state's three
most prominent commuter rail lines.

In February of 2015, a northbound Metro-North Railroad passenger train
collided with a sports utility vehicle that had stopped on the tracks.
This tragic accident resulted in the deaths of five passengers and the
vehicle's driver. While the presence of warning devices such as flashing
lights, signs, and gates have helped to prevent such catastrophes, they
have not adequately deterred drivers from failing to adhere to these
crucial safety measures.  Additionally, on May 4, 2015, a school bus at
Roaring Brook Road railroad crossing in Westchester County stopped only
inches from the tracks, which left just enough clearance from the pass-
ing train to avoid an accident. However, the driver failed to leave
enough room for the lowering gate and caused the bus to become trapped.
Since March 2014, there were thirty-eight tickets issued at this specif-
ic crossing for driving violations. These near miss situations bring
attention to the fact that aggressive or distracted drivers are failing
to comply with safety laws at railroad grade crossings and putting many
in danger.

This piece of legislation would aid in the effort to decrease the inci-
dence of vehicular accidents at railroad grade crossings by providing a
flexible mechanism to local and regional authorities to deter driving
violations that result in these horrific and costly collisions. Utiliz-
ing the same technology as red light cameras, railroad grade crossing
violation-monitoring systems will fine drivers who fail to adhere to
safety signals indicating an approaching train. This fine will incentiv-
ize drivers to pay particular attention to signs indicating appropriate
stopping distances from railroad crossings and thereby prevent serious
and deadly accidents.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-20: S.4089 (Thomas)/ A.6012(Abinanti)- Passed Senate.

2018: S.2303 (Murphy)/A.4795(Abinanti)-Referred to Transportation.

2017: S.2303 (Murphy)/A.4795(Abinanti)-Passed Senate.

2015-2016: S.5238 (Murphy) / A.7646 (Abinanti) - Passed Senate.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law, and it shall expire and be deemed repealed 5 years after
such effective date.
